name: Status-separated capital panels
reader_question: How much money sits at each transaction status, and how much of it has actually become binding or moved?
relationship: Amounts split by status in separate panels on one unit; a status is never added to another.
use_when: Announced, authorized, binding and drawn amounts are all stated and must not be conflated
The reader needs to see where an amount stops progressing through the status taxonomy
avoid_when: Statuses are not in the SMPT taxonomy
Amounts are in different currencies or on different bases — use parallel-basis-panels
A single total is requested — this pattern refuses to show one

data_contract.notes: One unit and currency for every panel
Taxonomy words in taxonomy order, one panel each
One amount per status; null means no amount stated, never zero
A cross-status total at data or row level fails integrity

units: One currency and unit; the scale is shared across panels and starts at zero. Nothing is added across panels.

editable: Bar shapes, labels, dashes and fills
not_data_bound: Bar lengths are drawn on a computed scale; values are not data-bound and no workbook is embedded
Hollow dashed outlines mark statuses before binding

table_alternative: A table of rows by status with blank cells for amounts not stated.
variations: Per-programme panels in place of per-organisation rows
limitations: A later status is not a subset of an earlier one unless the source says so, so bars are not read as conversion rates
Only taxonomy statuses are drawn; stages beyond expenditure need a different exhibit

excluded_alternatives.reason: Stacking adds amounts at different statuses into one total, which SMPT rules prohibit
Implies each status is a subset of the previous one and invites conversion-rate readings
